**Velocity loses meaning when AI inflates output.** Replying to a developer who claims a 10x output gain, practitioners recommend Monte Carlo forecasts from historical cycle times, range estimates that name the assumption which would break them, and tracking cycle time including rework together with failure demand. One team now runs out of planned sprint work, with manual QA as the new bottleneck. [Reddit r/projectmanagement, 25 Aug 2026](https://www.reddit.com/r/projectmanagement/comments/1vxxm0w/software_pms_how_do_you_measure_dev_velocity/)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-08-human-review-not-control" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-08/human-review-not-control/" data-aixpm-date="2026-08-31" data-aixpm-title="&quot;Human review&quot; is not a control in an AI risk register." markdown>

**"Human review" is not a control in an AI risk register.** A UK public-sector risk practitioner argues the entry says nothing about what the reviewer can see, verify and stop, citing court cases where a checked AI draft still went out wrong. He would send back any assessment listing it alone, and notes that the verification work lands on a few experienced staff rather than disappearing. [GovInsider, 24 Aug 2026](https://govinsider.asia/intl-en/article/if-your-ai-risk-register-says-human-review-send-it-back)
